title: Private deployments — access & audit mapping (RBAC v2 -> SIEM)
body:
Purpose and scope:
This note defines a compact reference for mapping RBAC v2 events and configuration state into our SIEM / evidence automation pipeline for private deployments. Focus: (1) RBAC role semantics and the audit events we need, (2) canonical audit/log schema for SIEM ingestion, (3) network segmentation and firewall templates to capture as evidence, (4) mTLS lifecycle checks and validation, (5) an automation runbook for evidence collection and retention. Audience: eng-private-deployments, security, compliance reviewers, SREs who run private installs.

Design principles (short):
- Immutable audit: every RBAC change and critical network config change must produce a verifiable, tamper-evident audit record (signed log lines or SIEM events with request_id and hash).
- Minimal noisy events: only emit high-signal events by default; enable verbose mode for audits and postmortems.
- Evidence-first: the pipeline should be able to answer the typical auditor questions in < 30 min: who changed what (role or firewall), when, from where, and what was the resulting state.

1) RBAC v2 quick-reference (roles + intent)
- platform-admin: full control over control-plane resources (deployments, routing, model pins). Audit needs: role grants, role revokes, permission additions, impersonation attempts.
- network-operator: manage VPC, firewall rules, peering, NAT/Egress configs. Audit needs: firewall create/update/delete, route table updates, subnet changes, peering config changes.
- auditor-readonly: can view configs and read audit logs only; no write. Audit needs: failed access attempts when trying writes.
- service-account (short-lived): used by control-plane components; should be constrained by labels: env=prod, tenant=<tenant-id>. Audit needs: token mint events, token revocation, unusual TTL extensions.
- dev-ops (limited): ephemeral elevated access via just-in-time (JIT) flow; must include approval id/CLAIM. Audit needs: JIT grant events, expiry, approver id.

Recommended RBAC semantics (practical):
- Prefer fine-grained resources over coarse roles (e.g., allow network-operator only on resource:VPC:team-x).
- All role grants must include an "approval_id" or "ticket_ref" if non-service-account; otherwise map to automated role assignment provisioning identity.
- Attach metadata labels (origin, ticket, justification) to every grant so logs carry context.

2) Canonical audit log schema (SIEM-friendly)
We emit structured JSON lines to the SIEM. Required fields (always):
- timestamp (ISO8601 UTC)
- event_type (rbac.grant | rbac.revoke | firewall.change | route.update | mtls.cert.rotate | auth.fail | auth.success)
- actor (string, human or service principal)
- actor_id (internal id)
- actor_roles (array as CSV string if needed)
- action (string verb)
- resource_type (VPC | SUBNET | FIREWALL_RULE | ROLE | TOKEN | CERT)
- resource_id (opaque id)
- outcome (success | failure | partial)
- request_id (trace id)
- src_ip (network origin)
- user_agent (client string)
- justification (ticket id / approval id)
- before_state_hash (sha256)
- after_state_hash (sha256)
- evidence_refs (CSV list of artifact ids or s3 paths)

Example JSON event (single-line) for a role grant:
{"timestamp":"2024-11-02T15:32:12Z","event_type":"rbac.grant","actor":"miguel.h","actor_id":"u-4892","actor_roles":"platform-admin","action":"grant","resource_type":"ROLE","resource_id":"role-network-operator-team-3","outcome":"success","request_id":"req-1fec3a","src_ip":"18.204.12.8","user_agent":"console/v2","justification":"JIRA-987","before_state_hash":"7b2c...","after_state_hash":"a9f1...","evidence_refs":"s3://redwood-evidence/private-deploys/2024-11-02/rbac-grant-role-network-operator-team-3.json"} 

Field guidance:
- before_state_hash and after_state_hash: compute against canonical config blob (sorted JSON bytes) so any auditor can fetch the referenced blob and verify.
- evidence_refs: point to immutable artifact (signed blob) stored under customer-controlled object storage for private installs.

3) Firewall / VPC canonical evidence items (what to capture)
For every firewall change capture:
- full rule-set snapshot (timestamped) as JSON (sorted by priority),
- single-rule diff (who/when/why),
- associated route-table snapshot and tags,
- SG / NSG translation and effective network policy (if cloud provider supports computed effective rules).

Firewall rule canonical template (cloud-friendly):
{
  "id": "fw-123456",
  "priority": "100",
  "action": "ALLOW|DENY",
  "direction": "INGRESS|EGRESS",
  "src": "10.0.0.0/16",
  "dst": "10.1.4.0/24",
  "protocol": "TCP|UDP|ICMP|ALL",
  "ports": "22,443-450",
  "created_by": "miguel.h",
  "created_at": "2024-10-01T14:04:00Z",
  "ticket_ref": "JIRA-1111",
  "comment": "allow control-plane -> model-pool metrics"
}
(Stored as canonical JSON; compute hash and emit event with evidence_ref.)

iptables example snippet (for on-prem installs):
-A PRIVATE-INGRESS -s 10.200.0.0/16 -d 10.10.0.0/24 -p tcp --dport 443 -m comment --comment "control-plane-metrics" -j ACCEPT

4) mTLS lifecycle & checks
Minimum requirements:
- client certs: 1 yr max TTL for long-lived service-accounts; better: 90-day TTL with automated rotation.
- CA: internal CA for private installs; CA root stored in HSM/KMS for production auditors.
- cipher preferences: TLS1.3 preferred; if TLS1.2 needed, configure to disallow legacy ciphers (RC4, 3DES).
- require cert transparency into SIEM: emit mtls.cert.present event with cert_serial and subject and expiry.

Key audit events for mTLS:
- mtls.cert.issue (who, csr_kid, cert_serial, ttl_days)
- mtls.cert.rotate (old_serial -> new_serial, rotation_trigger: expiry|compromise|manual)
- mtls.cert.revoke (serial, reason)
- mtls.tls.handshake_failure (src_ip, dst, reason, cert_serial_if_present)

OpenSSL commands for quick validation:
- inspect certificate: openssl x509 -in cert.pem -noout -subject -issuer -serial -dates
- verify chain: openssl verify -CAfile ca.pem cert.pem
- extract serial in hex: openssl x509 -noout -serial -in cert.pem

mTLS rotation automation sketch (high level):
- nightly job: list service certs -> for any expiring within 14 days, create CSR via service agent -> sign with intermediate CA -> store new cert in secrets manager -> push k/v to workload -> verify health-check endpoint confirms new cert in use -> emit mtls.cert.rotate event.
- On any failed handshake spike: create an incident, snapshot peer certs observed in TLS handshakes for 72 hours, export to s3 evidence bucket.

5) SIEM detection rules (examples)
- RBAC escalation: any rbac.grant where actor_role != "platform-admin" and resource_type == ROLE and granted_role == "platform-admin" => alert and require manual review (create SEC-incident).
- Firewall override: firewall.change where priority <= 100 and action == ALLOW and src == 0.0.0.0/0 => high severity alert plus automated revert if flagged by policy.
- Cert expiry delta: mtls.cert.present where days_until_expiry < 7 and cert_subject not in "exclude-on-call" list => notify owner and create JIRA.
- JIT bypass: role grant with claim_source == "jit" and missing approval_id => critical (possible bug or attacker).

6) Evidence automation runbook (practical steps)
Goal: within 2 hours produce a compliance package for an auditor request covering a specified time window.
Inputs: customer-id, time-window, requestor-email, ticket-id.
Steps:
1) validate authorization (ticket_id mapping) and record request_id.
2) collect RBAC events for time-window from audit-topic (kinesis/kafka) -> filter by customer id -> write to signed blob (canonical sorted JSON) -> compute hash and store at evidence path.
3) collect firewall snapshots + diffs -> canonicalize -> sign -> store.
4) collect network flow logs (VPC flow logs / fw logs) for time-window -> run automated summarization to identify DNAT/ASN anomalies -> store raw + summary.
5) collect mTLS cert events and handshake failures -> attach openssl extracts for certs observed.
6) produce manifest.json listing blobs + hashes + verifier public key.
7) push manifest and blobs to the customer evidence bucket (s3://customer-evidence/<customer>/requests/<request_id>/).
8) emit siem.event evidence.package.created with manifest_ref.

Retention & tamper-evidence: all artifacts must be signed with a rotation-aware signing key. Signing key metadata (key id, creation time) is recorded in the manifest. Retention policy: default 1 year for private deployment evidence; customers can opt for 3/7 years as per contract.

7) Network segmentation diagram (ascii)
[Internet] --> [Egress / WAF / NAT] --> [Ingress buffer / Bastion] --> 
    --> [Control-plane zone] <---> [Model-serving zone (isolated per-tenant)]
                        \--> [Metrics/Observability zone (read-only access from model-serving)]
Notes: Control-plane zone must be separate VPC peering or VPC with strict firewall rules; no direct inbound from internet to model-serving.

8) Pre-deploy checklist (minimal)
- [ ] create immutable audit-topic and test event sign/verify flow
- [ ] provision initial RBAC roles + record ticket refs
- [ ] baseline firewall snapshot (store hash) and tag with deployment id
- [ ] install mTLS CA and load root into KMS/HSM
- [ ] enable VPC flow logs and verify SIEM ingestion pipeline
- [ ] configure evidence bucket with write-only signing principal and retention lifecycle

Quarterly audit tasks:
- rotate root signing key (generate new key, sign manifest, publish new verifier key)
- run RBAC least-privilege scan and remediate stale grants older than 90 days
- run firewall effective-policy sweep to detect overly permissive rules
- check expired certs and validate rotation job health

9) Outputs for auditors (naming conventions)
- rbac-events-<customer>-<requestid>-<ts>.ndjson (gzip)
- firewall-snapshot-<customer>-<deployment>-<ts>.json (signed)
- mtls-certs-archive-<customer>-<requestid>.tar.gz (signed, contains openssl extracts)
- manifest-<requestid>.json (contains all blobs + hashes + signing key id)

Open questions (to resolve before finalizing):
- For on-prem installs, do we standardize on a single signing scheme (JSON Web Signature v2) or allow HSM-signed binary manifests? (security prefers HSM-bound signatures).
- Where do we persist long-term encryption keys for archived evidence for customers with >3 year retention? (KMS with key rotation policy or customer-supplied HSM?)
- Should the SIEM pipeline keep raw event payloads for 90 days by default or only summaries + signed blobs? (cost vs forensics tradeoff).

References and quick wins:
- Confluence: Private Deployments Security Index (linked above)
- RFC: audit-log-schema-v1 (see github PR above)
- Quick win: enable mtls.cert.present events in verbose mode for one customer for 30 days and verify alerting on expiry < 7d.

Notes to reviewers: this is a working reference. My ask: please flag missing events you routinely need for audits and any provider-specific translation rules (Azure NSG vs AWS SG vs GCP firewall) you want included.
